title: セイバールート十四日目-11

pages.ja:
最後に。
もう一度、あの赤い丘を見る。
pages.jaRuby:
最後に。
もう一度、あの赤い丘を見る。
pages.en:
—One last time—

I see that scarlet hill.

pages.ja:
赤い記憶。
以前より深く彼女の記憶に沈んで、同時に、これが最後なのだと感じていた。
pages.jaRuby:
赤い記憶。
以前より深く彼女の記憶に沈んで、同時に、これが最後なのだと感じていた。
pages.en:
A memory steeped in red.

I sink more deeply into her past than ever before, knowing all the while that this will be the last time.

pages.ja:
それはもう何度も見てきた、ある騎士の記憶。
国王となり、自分の意思を殺して国の意思となり、信頼できる騎士たちから疎まれるようになった日々。
pages.jaRuby:
それはもう何度も見てきた、ある騎士の記憶。
国王となり、自分の意思を殺して国の意思となり、信頼できる[ruby text=とも o2o=1]騎士たちから疎まれるようになった日々。
pages.en:
It is the memory of a knight I have seen many times.

She became king, killed her own will to embody the will of her country, and lived to see the trusted knights who had been her friends come to loathe her.

pages.ja:
戦に勝利する度に、望まぬ戦いを望まれたアルトリア。
女性である事を隠し続け、不審を買い、孤立した彼女に待っていたものは、肉親による謀反だった。
pages.jaRuby:

女性である事を隠し続け、不審を買い、孤立した彼女に待っていたものは、肉親による謀反だった。
pages.en:
With every victory, Altria was called upon to fight another war she did not want.

She concealed her sex, inviting suspicion and isolation. What awaited her at the end was a rebellion led by her own blood.

pages.ja:
遠征に出た王の留守を狙い、国を乗っ取った若い騎士。
男の名はモードレッド。
騎士王の姉モルガンの息子であるその騎士は、その実、騎士王の息子だった。

pages.en:
A young knight seized the country while its king was away on campaign.

His name was Mordred.

The son of Morgan, the King of Knights' sister—yet in truth, he was the King of Knights' own son.

pages.ja:
結論から言えば、女性であるアルトリアに子を作る事は出来ない。
だが、確かにモードレッドはアルトリアの血を受け継いではいたのだ。
アルトリアの姉であるモルガン
妹でありながら王となったアルトリアを恨む彼女の妄念が、どのような手を尽くしたのか定かではない。

pages.en:
—To state the obvious, Altria was a woman and could not have fathered a child.

And yet Mordred unquestionably carried her blood.

Morgan was Altria's elder sister, consumed by hatred for the younger sister who had become king. No one knows what means that obsession drove her to employ.

pages.ja: 彼女の分身として作られたモードレッドは、父を明かせぬ騎士として王に仕え、その座を簒奪する日を待ち、ついに反旗を翻した。

pages.en: Created as Altria's duplicate, Mordred served the king as a knight who could never reveal his father. He waited for the day he could usurp the throne, and at last raised the banner of rebellion.

pages.ja:
後にカムランの戦いと呼ばれる、
アーサー王最後の戦いである。
pages.jaRuby:
後にカムランの戦いと呼ばれる、
アーサー王最後の戦いである。
pages.en:
—It would come to be called the Battle of Camlann:

the final battle of King Arthur.

pages.ja:
遠征先でモードレッドの裏切りを知ったアーサー王は、疲れきった兵を連れて国に戻り、自らの領土へ侵攻した。
かつて従えていた騎士をことごとく斬り伏せ、
自身が守っていた土地に攻め入った。
かろうじて自分に付き従ってくれた騎士たちも散っていき、最後に残ったのは、自身と、息子である騎士だけだった。

pages.en:
King Arthur learned of Mordred's treachery while on campaign. Leading her exhausted soldiers home, she invaded her own country.

She cut down the knights who had once served her.

She marched upon the land she had protected.

The few knights who remained faithful fell one after another, until only two figures stood upon the field: the king and the knight who was, in form at least, her son.

pages.ja:
両者の一騎打ちは、王の勝利で幕を下ろした。
……だが、無傷だったという訳ではない。
強い呪いでくくられたモードレッドは死してなお剣を振るい、王に、もはや癒せない傷を残したからだ。
それがこの戦いの終わり。
騎士王と言われた彼女の、最後の姿だった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Their duel ended in the king's victory.

…But she did not escape unwounded.

Bound by a terrible curse, Mordred struck with his sword even in death and left the king a wound no power could heal.

Thus the battle ended.

That was the final image of the woman called the King of Knights.

pages.ja:
辛くなかった筈はない。
思えば、彼女の戦いで辛くないものなどなかった。
十二もの戦いはそのどれもが身を削くような戦いであり、これは、その最後に相応しい、もっとも大きな傷跡に他ならない。

pages.en:
—It must have hurt.

When I think of it, not one of her wars could have been anything but painful.

Each of the twelve battles carved away a part of her. This last was the deepest scar of all, a wound fit to mark their end.

pages.ja:
領地に戻り、自国の軍を蹴散らし。
臣下であった騎士を自らの手で処罰し、従ってくれた騎士たちを皆死なせ。
その果てに、カタチの上であれ、息子であった騎士を倒さねばならなかった。

pages.en:
She returned to her own land and crushed her country's army.

She punished former vassals with her own hands and watched every knight who remained loyal die.

At the end of it all, she was forced to kill the knight who, however unnaturally, was her son.

pages.ja:
……その胸に去来したものが何であるか、俺には知るよしもない。
ただ、願ってしまった。
最後まで王として在り続けようとした、一人の騎士。
その死の直前に見た夢が、せめて
アルトリアという少女が望んだ、当たり前の夢であるようにと。

pages.en:
…I cannot know what passed through her heart.

I can only wish.

For the solitary knight who remained a king until the end.

May the dream she saw on the verge of death have been, at least, an ordinary dream desired by the girl named Altria.

pages.ja:
「ん……」
目蓋を開ける。
いつの間にか帰ってきたのか。自分の部屋にいて、布団の上に寝かされていた。

pages.en:
“Mm…”

My eyes open.

When did we return? I am in my own room, lying upon the futon.

pages.ja:
「
ああ。気が付いたのですね、シロウ」
「……セイバー、俺は、どうして」
「あれから今まで眠っていたのです。身体の方はほぼ完治してますから、心配には及びません」

pages.en:
“—You are awake, Shirou.”

“…Saber? What happened to me?”

“You have slept ever since. Your body is almost completely healed, so there is no cause for alarm.”

pages.ja:
「……そうか。それは、いいけど」
セイバーの方はどうなのか。
今はエクスカリバーを使った後だ。自然治癒の為の魔力も不足しているのではないだろうか。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…I see. That's good, but…”

What about Saber?

She used Excalibur. Surely she is short even of the magical energy required to heal herself.

pages.ja:
「セイバー、ずっと俺の手当を？」
「手当といっても汗を拭く程度です。私は凛の様に、人の傷を診る事はできませんから」
pages.jaRuby:
「セイバー、ずっと俺の手当を？」

pages.en:
“Saber, have you been tending to me this whole time?”

“I have done little more than wipe away your sweat. Unlike Rin, I cannot examine and treat another person's wounds.”

pages.ja:
「
ばか。そんなことしなくていいんだ。
今は俺より、セイバーの方が辛いだろう」
pages.jaRuby:

ばか。そんなことしなくていいんだ。
今は俺より、セイバーの方が辛いだろう」
pages.en:
“—Idiot. You don't need to do that.

“You're the one who must be suffering now.”

pages.ja:
「そのような事はありません。シロウに比べれば、私は軽傷です。
しかし、今のは聞き捨てなりませんね。いくら傷が塞がったといっても、シロウは死んでもおかしくない傷だったのです。今は自分の身体を案じてください」

pages.en:
“That is not so. Compared with you, my injuries are slight.

“And I cannot ignore what you just said. Though your wounds have closed, they could easily have killed you. For now, attend to your own body.”

pages.en:
Saber reaches for a washbasin beside her.

A single towel rests in chilled water. She wrings it out, then wipes the sweat from my body.

“—”

The embarrassment is almost unbearable.

pages.ja:
「？ シロウ、傷が痛むのですか？ また熱が出て来たようですが
」
pages.jaRuby:
「？ シロウ、傷が痛むのですか？ また熱が出て来たようですが
」
pages.en: “Hm? Does your wound hurt, Shirou? You seem to be growing feverish again—”

pages.ja:
「ね、熱なんか出てないっ……！ いや、そうじゃなくて、いいからセイバーも休んでくれ。
今は元気かもしれないけど、エクスカリバーを使ったんだ。セイバーの方こそ休んでなくちゃダメじゃないか。そんなんじゃまた倒れちまうだろう」

pages.en:
“I-I don't have a fever…! No, never mind that. Saber, you need to rest.

“You may feel fine now, but you used Excalibur. You're the one who should be in bed. If you keep this up, you'll collapse again.”

pages.ja: 「え……まぁ、それは、そうなのですが……」
pages.jaRuby: 「え……まぁ、それは、そうなのですが……」
pages.en: “Well… yes, that may be true…”

pages.ja:
「今は私の方が元気ですから。マスターの傷が癒えるまで、私が守るのが当然でしょう」
「う……それは、もっともな話、だよな」
pages.jaRuby:
「今は私の方が元気ですから。マスターの傷が癒えるまで、私が守るのが当然でしょう」
「う……それは、もっともな話、だよな」
pages.en:
“At present, I am the stronger of us. It is only natural that I protect my Master until his wounds have healed.”

“Uh… I suppose that does make sense.”

pages.ja:
……まいった。
そんな顔でそんなコトを言われたら、納得するしかないじゃないか。
pages.jaRuby:
……まいった。
そんな顔でそんなコトを言われたら、納得するしかないじゃないか。
pages.en:
…I surrender.

When she says something like that with such an expression, I have no choice but to agree.

pages.ja:
「わかったよ。俺もしっかりと休むから、セイバーもちゃんと休んでくれ。セイバーが休んでくれないと、俺も落ち着いて眠れない」
「それは……そうですね。私とて睡眠を取らねばならぬ身ですから」
pages.jaRuby:
「わかったよ。俺もしっかりと休むから、セイバーもちゃんと休んでくれ。セイバーが休んでくれないと、俺も落ち着いて眠れない」
「それは……そうですね。私とて睡眠を取らねばならぬ身ですから」
pages.en:
“All right. I'll rest properly, so you have to do the same. If you don't sleep, I won't be able to relax either.”

“That is… true. I too possess a body that requires sleep.”

pages.ja:
セイバーはあっさりと頷いて、最後にタオルを絞ると洗面器に掛けた。
……そうして。照れくささを堪えながら、セイバーの看病を見守った。

pages.en:
Saber agrees readily. She wrings out the towel one final time and drapes it over the rim of the basin.

…And so, enduring my embarrassment, I allow Saber to finish nursing me.

pages.ja:
「それでは、私も先に休ませて頂きます。
御身、くれぐれもお大事に、シロウ」
「あ、ああ」
「
おやすみなさい。
言いそびれましたが、礼を言いますシロウ。
貴方が助かって、本当に良かった」

pages.en:
“Then I will retire before you.

“Please take the greatest care of yourself, Shirou.”

“Y-yeah.”

“—Good night.

“There is one thing I neglected to say. Thank you, Shirou.

“I am truly glad that you survived.”

pages.ja:
セイバーが月明かりの中で、笑っていた。
微かに儚げに見えたのは、消え入りそうな月明かりの陰影のせいか。
それを確かめるまでもなく、コトリ、と襖は閉じた。

pages.en:
Saber smiles in the moonlight.

If she seems faint and fragile, perhaps it is only the shadow cast by that fading light.

Before I can discover the truth, the sliding door closes with a quiet click.

“……………Whew.”

Saber disappears into the bedroom. Am I relieved or lonely?

Part of me wishes she had remained at my bedside, but that would only place a greater burden upon her.

…Besides, being alone with Saber in circumstances like these feels too much like that night—

…I drive the image from my mind.

Too much happened today. It was only one day, yet it feels as long as a week.

My date with Saber was more difficult than enjoyable. In the end, we argued, and I left her alone.

And then—

“—”

…No. I have to rest and recover my strength. I can think afterward.

It is not only Gilgamesh. We still do not know the identities of Lancer or his Master.

If we are to survive, I must wake and begin again in perfect condition.

“—”

That happened only a few hours ago.

…Saber said something about me being her scabbard.

I was half destroyed and seconds from sleep, so I never managed to ask what she meant.

“…Oh, enough.”

I cannot fall asleep.

…The Saber in my dream—her face proud and unwavering even before death—overlaps the Saber who tended to me.

*Good night.*

The fragile smile she offered refuses to leave my eyes.

“………………”

A smile that never once appeared on the face of the girl in my dream.

She says that seeing me smile makes her happier than smiling herself.

…And that frustrates me beyond endurance.

Why frustration rather than sorrow?

I cannot understand the anger twisting inside me.

I strike the futon with my fist.

The shapeless frustration makes me want to tear the room apart.

“…Shirou? Are you feeling unwell?”

Saber's worried voice reaches me through the sliding door.

My breathing was ragged. She must think I turned over in pain.

“…No, I'm fine. More importantly, are you still awake?”

“Yes, but… are you certain you are well? If you are still in pain, I will come to you.”

If I see Saber now, whatever I have restrained will overflow.

“…Saber. Can we talk for a minute?”

“Hm? Yes, if you do not mind speaking this way…”

We begin with the sliding door between us.

Unable to see her, I picture the smile she wore when we parted.

ただ、セイバーと話さないと。
それは違うと。俺は本当に正しい事を知らずとも、その事だけは、間違っていないと伝えないと。

…Saber smiling with genuine happiness.

The memory does not soothe my frustration. It makes it worse.

I do not understand why my body burns like this.

I only know that I must speak to her.

I must tell her that she is wrong. I may not know what is truly right, but of that one thing, I am certain.

My throat and tongue tremble.

Once I say the words, there will be no taking them back.

Knowing that completely—

“—Enough. You have to smile for your own sake now.”

Driven by an impulse I cannot name, I bite off each word.

I force down the passion that surges without warning.

The dam is seconds from breaking.

If only Saber will say one word before it does.

“…Shirou. Please do not torment me.

“Even if you say such things, I—I…”

—Her answer has not changed.

The immovable certainty in her voice constricts my heart.

“Why do you concern yourself with me so deeply?

“…You have seen how many sins I committed.”

In the name of kingship, she sacrificed many lives and killed countless enemies.

I will neither overlook those acts nor pretend they never happened.

And even knowing them, I still want the girl named Altria to be happy.

Those are not the words of the girl named Altria. They are the lonely oath of someone resolved to remain a king.

I know all of that already.

I did not feel all this furious frustration merely to hear that cry again.

I felt nothing like this then.

…How absurd.

All this time, I pursued the dream of becoming a Hero of Justice—

without ever knowing what it meant to cherish someone, or to be unable to let them go.

My happiness outweighs my embarrassment.

Saber rises.

I am reluctant to release her, but we cannot remain this way. I walk toward the open sliding door.

For some reason, I wait upon the futon in formal seiza.

One thought dances ceaselessly through my head: I am going to sleep beside Saber. It is for the sake of helping her, and it will grant one of her small wishes.

If such wishes continue to accumulate, perhaps one day Saber will learn to smile.

…But the war is nearing its climax. How much time can possibly remain to us?

A figure in white, floating in the darkness.

The sight stills every restless emotion inside me.

The agitation drains from my heart, leaving it clear and wakeful.

I should have no indecent intentions, yet my face feels ready to burst into flame. I cannot even steal a glance at her.

Her warmth and faint fragrance do not quicken my heart. They quiet it into peace.

Because we chose to fight in order to bring this war to an end.

There is no answer I can make to that.

Before we can resolve what lies between us, we must end the battle before us.

More than that, until we defeat the man pursuing Saber, there is no question of protecting her at all.

—But—

do we possess any means of defeating the King of Heroes?

It does not matter if it is only a momentary weakness permitted for this one night.

Her hand is warm within mine.

—The end of the battle.

Without knowing whether, once everything is over, I will still be able to hold this hand—

quietly.
